developments: Asian shares followed Wall Street lower, with the Nikkei down 1.2%, the Hang Seng down 1.2% and the Kospi down 1% to 2% on chip-stock weakness before Nvidia's results, AP and Reuters reported.
Bitcoin gave back Monday evening's gain, slipping to about $64,380 on Kraken by 06:30 UK from about $65,150 at the evening edition, inside an overnight range of roughly $64,320 to $65,470.
The Zcash Foundation released Zebra 7.1.0, fixing ten security advisories, and told node, miner, exchange and wallet-server operators to upgrade now.
briefing.changed: Little changed for prices overnight: bitcoin drifted about $800 lower, Zcash edged up to about $915, and Asian shares extended the AI sell-off while US futures steadied slightly higher. The dollar index touched its highest since April 2025. Monday's ETF flow figures were still not out.
briefing.question: Will Nvidia's results tonight steady the AI sell-off or deepen it, and will bitcoin keep its distance from tech shares either way?
briefing.watch: US retail sales at 13:30 UK, Fed Governor Waller at about 14:10 UK, then Nvidia's results after the US close, about 21:20 UK. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

lead.headline: Asia follows Wall Street lower as bitcoin slips before Nvidia
lead.standfirst: Regional stock markets fell around 1% overnight on chip weakness, and bitcoin gave back Monday evening's gain to trade near $64,400.
body: Asian shares fell on Tuesday as the sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks spread from Wall Street. Japan's Nikkei 225 lost 1.2%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 1.2% and Australia's ASX 200 dropped 1.5%, the Associated Press reported. SoftBank fell 6.2%.
MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was down 1.2%, Reuters reported, while US stock futures edged up, with Nasdaq futures 0.35% higher.
Bitcoin drifted lower through the Asian session. It traded near $64,380 on Kraken at 06:30 UK, down from about $65,150 at the US close, after moving between roughly $64,320 and $65,470 overnight.

The dollar rose to its highest level since April 2025, Reuters reported, as markets priced a Federal Reserve rate rise in December as all but certain. CME FedWatch showed about 91% odds of a quarter-point rise and 9% for half a point on Monday evening, Cryptoticker reported.

Nvidia reports third-quarter results after the US close on Tuesday, its first since Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive. Interim chief executive Colette Kress is due to speak, AP reported. US retail sales figures are due at 13:30 UK.

headline: Asian shares fell about 1% on chip weakness and the dollar hit a 19-month high, while bitcoin slipped to about $64,400. Nvidia's results tonight are the day's big test.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, morning edition. Asian shares followed Wall Street lower overnight, with Japan and Hong Kong both down about one percent as chip stocks slid before Nvidia's results. The dollar hit its highest since April last year. Bitcoin gave back last night's gain and is near sixty-four thousand four hundred dollars. Zcash is steady at about nine hundred and fifteen dollars, and its node software Zebra has an urgent security update for operators. Today, US retail sales at half past one, then Nvidia's results at about twenty past nine this evening, UK time. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Asian shares follow Wall Street's chip sell-off
stories.why: The Nikkei fell 1.2%, the Hang Seng 1.2%, the ASX 200 1.5% and the Taiex 0.9%, AP reported, with SoftBank down 6.2%. Reuters put MSCI Asia ex-Japan down 1.2% and the Kospi down 2% early. US futures were slightly higher, with Nasdaq futures up 0.35%.
stories.caveat: AP had the Kospi down 1% while Reuters reported 2% shortly after the open; the figure moved during the session.

note.read: The AI de-risking that hit Wall Street on Monday carried through Asia; firmer US futures suggest traders are waiting for Nvidia rather than selling further.
note.alt: Asia may simply be catching up with Monday's US close, with no new selling pressure behind it.
note.change: A strong Nvidia report tonight and a Nasdaq rebound would ease the pressure on risk assets including bitcoin.

stories.title: Bitcoin slips back to about $64,400 overnight
stories.why: Bitcoin traded near $64,380 on Kraken at 06:30 UK, down about $800 from the evening edition, after an overnight range of roughly $64,320 to $65,470. It remains above Monday's low near $63,840 and well below the 200-week average near $68,200 cited by Cointelegraph. CoinDesk reported on Monday that Nvidia's results could push bitcoin below $60,000 if they deepen the risk sell-off.

note.read: Bitcoin's late Monday resilience faded in thin Asian trade but it has not broken down; the range is holding ahead of tonight's results.
note.alt: The dip may reflect the stronger dollar rather than equities, which would make Fed pricing the bigger driver.
note.change: A break below Monday's low near $63,840, or a large ETF outflow figure for Monday when it is published.

stories.title: Dollar hits highest since April 2025 as December hike is priced in
stories.why: The dollar index peaked at 103.69, its highest since April 2025, and the yen sat near 160, Reuters reported, with markets treating a December Fed rate rise as certain. CME FedWatch showed about 91% odds of a quarter-point rise and 9% of half a point on Monday evening, Cryptoticker reported. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to 5.13%, AP said. A strong dollar has weighed on bitcoin all month.
stories.caveat: FedWatch odds come from a single crypto outlet's reading on Monday evening and move daily.

note.read: With a hike priced in, the open question has narrowed to its size; that keeps the dollar firm and is a headwind for bitcoin.
note.alt: If the hike is fully priced, any softer US data could weaken the dollar quickly and relieve pressure.
note.change: Weak retail sales today, or Fed speakers leaning against a half-point move.

stories.title: Zebra 7.1.0 patches ten security flaws; operators told to upgrade now
stories.why: The Zcash Foundation's Zebra 7.1.0 fixes ten advisories, mostly ways a peer could stall a node's sync or exhaust its memory. Node operators, miners, pools, exchanges and wallet servers should upgrade now; no resync is needed and ZEC holders have nothing to do. Zcash traded near $915 on Kraken at 06:30 UK, up from about $900 at the evening edition.

stories.title: Community panel poll opens on Zcash grants funding (NU7.1)
stories.why: The Zcash Foundation opened an advisory poll of its community panel on how Zcash Community Grants is funded, with options from winding it down and sending its 8% stream to a dev and legal-defence lockbox, to keeping it as is. It also asks about shorter block times. The poll closes at 02:59 UK on Tuesday 1 December and runs alongside the grants vote reported on Monday.

stories.title: Cypherpunk adds 3,775 ZEC, holds over 2% of supply
stories.why: Winklevoss-backed Cypherpunk Technologies bought 3,775 ZEC at an average of $920.40, taking its treasury above 341,858 ZEC, just over 2% of circulating supply, The Block reported. Its new mining arm made $2.6 million of operating profit in its first quarter. A large single holder matters for ZEC's thin market.

stories.title: Trezor customer shipping data leaked again
stories.why: Names, phone numbers, emails and delivery addresses from about 27,000 Trezor orders placed between 9 August and 7 November were exposed at shipping partner Skladon, The Block and Decrypt reported. Trezor says no wallet backups, PINs or passphrases leaked, but warns of phishing calls and physical-security risk.

explained.title: Why a strong dollar weighs on bitcoin
body: Bitcoin is priced in dollars. When the dollar strengthens, usually because US interest rates are expected to rise, holding cash or Treasuries pays more and dollar-priced assets look dearer to buyers elsewhere.

That is why a dollar index at a 19-month high and a priced-in Fed rise have gone hand in hand with bitcoin's slide this month. For a UK holder, a stronger dollar also means the sterling value of bitcoin falls less than the dollar price.

investigating: Did spot bitcoin ETF outflows continue on Monday 16 November? Evidence: Farside and SoSoValue daily figures, still unpublished at 06:30 UK.
Is bitcoin decoupling from tech shares or just lagging them? Evidence: how it trades through Nvidia's results tonight and Wednesday's Nasdaq open.
